headline: 35 years later, Presidential election voting begins in Bangladesh
summary: Members of Parliament are casting their votes for the 23rd President of Bangladesh, marking the first contested election in over three decades.
details: Voting for the 23rd President of Bangladesh began at 2:00 PM on Thursday (August 20) at the National Parliament House session room.
Members of Parliament from both the ruling party and the opposition are exercising their right to vote in this election.
Two candidates are contesting this election: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir of the ruling BNP and Oli Ahmed of the 11-party alliance representing the opposition.
This is the first contested presidential election in 35 years since the parliamentary system of government was reintroduced in 1991.
Previously, seven consecutive presidents had been elected unopposed, ending a long period of uncontested appointments.
Voting will continue until 5:00 PM today. The Election Commission will announce the results after the counting process is complete.
The elected president is scheduled to take the oath of office tomorrow, Friday (August 21).

headline_marked: Gold prices rise again: [[22K gold now 240,628 BDT per bhori]]
headline: Gold prices rise again: 22K gold now 240,628 BDT per bhori
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association has increased gold prices due to rising global market trends, affecting all gold purity levels.
details: Gold prices in Bangladesh have increased by 3,849 BDT per bhori, effective from Thursday morning. The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJewS) BAJewS announced the hike in a notice issued at 10:00 AM.
Following the price adjustment, the price of high-quality 22-carat gold has risen to 240,628 BDT per bhori. 21-carat gold now costs 229,781 BDT, while 18-carat gold stands at 197,355 BDT.
Traditional gold prices have also increased by 2,566 BDT, reaching 161,196 BDT per bhori. The price hike is primarily driven by the increase in gold prices in the international market.
This is the second increase in a short period, following a previous hike on August 15, where prices rose by a maximum of 2,158 BDT. At that time, 22-carat gold was priced at 236,779 BDT.
The highest price ever recorded in the country's market has been 286,000 BDT per bhori, which occurred on January 29 of this year when prices jumped by 16,213 BDT in a single day.
In addition to gold, silver prices have also increased. The price of high-quality 22-carat silver has risen by 233 BDT, bringing the total price to 5,307 BDT per bhori.
